Container.Name: socket-proxy
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: docker socket proxy security traefik dozzle homepage allowlist
Container.Overview:
A lightweight, secure-by-default proxy for the Docker socket. Containers that need to read Docker (Traefik, Dozzle, Homepage, Telegraf, n8n) connect to this proxy over TCP instead of mounting /var/run/docker.sock themselves, and the proxy only passes through the exact API calls you allow.
Everything is denied until you allow it: set "Allowed Clients" and at least the GET allowlist below, or no client will get through. Allowlists are Go regular expressions, one per HTTP method (a leading ^ and trailing $ are added for you).
How other containers use it: put them on the same custom Docker network as this container (name lookup does not work on the default bridge), remove their docker.sock mount, and point them at http://socket-proxy:2375 (for example DOCKER_HOST=tcp://socket-proxy:2375). Do not publish the port to your LAN and never expose it to the internet.
Traefik 2.11.31 / 3.6.1 and later also need HEAD /_ping allowed. Coming from the Tecnativa or LinuxServer docker-socket-proxy? The converter at https://socket-proxy-configurator.wollomatic.dev/ turns their environment variables into allowlists.
This template runs the container as root (Extra Parameters: --user 0:0) because the image's default user (65534) cannot open the root-owned Docker socket on Unraid. It is also run read-only with all capabilities dropped. For least privilege, check the socket's group with ls -l /var/run/docker.sock and use --user 65534:<that group id> instead.

Config.Name: Docker Socket
Config.Description: Host Docker socket the proxy filters. Mounted read-only; the API filtering is done by the allowlists below, not by this mount mode.

Config.Name: Allowed Clients
Config.Description: Container names or CIDRs allowed to connect, comma-separated. Examples: traefik,dozzle or 172.18.0.0/16. Required: the default only allows localhost, so nothing else could connect.

Config.Name: Allow GET
Config.Description: Regex of allowed GET paths. Traefik example: /v1\..{1,2}/(version|containers/.*|events.*) . Log and container reading only: /(v1\..{1,2}/)?containers/(json|[^/]+/logs)

Config.Name: Allow HEAD
Config.Description: Regex of allowed HEAD paths. Traefik 2.11.31 / 3.6.1 and later need /_ping. Leave empty if the client does not use HEAD.

Config.Name: Allow POST
Config.Description: Regex of allowed POST paths. Leave empty to keep the proxy read-only. POST can start, stop, create and exec containers, so only allow exactly what a trusted client needs (for example a restart-only proxy: /containers/[^/]+/restart).

Config.Name: Listen IP
Config.Description: Address the proxy binds inside the container. Must be 0.0.0.0 for other containers to reach it.

Config.Name: Proxy Port
Config.Description: TCP port the proxy listens on inside the container. Not published to the host by this template.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR. DEBUG logs every request, which is the easy way to find out which API calls a client needs.

Config.Name: Watchdog Interval
Config.Description: Check every N seconds that the Docker socket still answers (0 disables). Useful after a Docker engine update.

Config.Name: Stop On Watchdog
Config.Description: Stop the container when the watchdog finds the socket unavailable, so the restart policy brings it back with a fresh connection.

Config.Name: Allowed Bind Mounts
Config.Description: Optional, comma-separated host directories that clients may bind-mount in container-create requests, for example /mnt/user/appdata. Only matters if you allow POST.

Config.Name: Proxy Container Name
Config.Description: Optional. Set to this container's own name to read per-client allowlists from Docker labels (socket-proxy.allow.get and so on) on each client container instead of one global list.
